cues.text: In the last video, I said any quantum computation boils down to a vector times a matrix. But that's not how people usually draw quantum computations.
Instead, they draw a horizontal line for each qubit, and gates where the qubits interact.
This diagram is meant to be closer to how the quantum computer exists physically, with time going from left to right.
But you just have to know, in the back of your mind, that it can be converted in a mechanical way into a vector times a matrix. So let's do that.
Three wires means three qubits, so 2 to the 3, or 8 possible states, just like the 3 tape cells last time.
Each gate has its own little matrix: 2 by 2 for a gate on one wire, and 4 by 4 for a gate on two wires.
To turn a little matrix into a big 8 by 8 one, we copy it in, once for each setting of the wires the gate doesn't touch.
That's because a gate only mixes states that differ on its own wires, and leaves the other wires alone.
Then we just multiply the vector by each gate's big matrix, one after another.
And since we write the vector as a row, the matrices even come in the same order as the gates in the diagram.
Or we can multiply the big matrices all together first, and the whole diagram becomes one big matrix.
So the diagram is really just a compact way of writing down a giant matrix: a few lines, instead of 2 to the n rows and columns.

script.dir: the 8 states 000…111 (each bit in its wire’s color) · the vector: a 1 at 000

script.dir: H’s 2×2 and CNOT’s 4×4 appear under the diagram (a beat)

script.dir: the big 8×8 appears; H’s four entries fly in, 4 times, one per setting of the other two wires (a beat)

script.text: That's because a gate only mixes states that differ on its own wires, and leaves the other wires alone.
script.dir: the four copies light up in turn: H only mixes 0xy ↔ 1xy (a long beat)

script.text: Then we just multiply the vector by each gate's big matrix, one after another.
script.dir: three steps, the cursor walks the diagram: 000 → (000+100)/√2 → (000+110)/√2 → (000+111)/√2 (a long beat)

script.text: And since we write the vector as a row, the matrices even come in the same order as the gates in the diagram.

script.dir: a box around the whole diagram; the matrix becomes M₁·M₂·M₃; one step gives the same result ✓
